assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks combine Katori's magic-wavelength proposal with Lamb-Dicke-regime trapping of many neutral atoms, giving fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and below. This is a clear, original and field-defining advance in precision measurement, and it underpins relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and the planned redefinition of the second. It is laser spectroscopy at its best.
assessment.attribution: Katori originated the lattice-clock concept and the magic wavelength; Ye's group realized and pushed the strontium clocks to record accuracy and demonstrated gravitational redshift at millimetre scale. The two names support a clean two-person prize, though ion-clock and frequency-comb work is already recognized (Hall and Hansch 2005; Wineland 2012) and others may deserve some credit.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by many laboratories (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE, NPL) with agreed uncertainties and international clock comparisons. The interpretation is stable and the field is mature, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would require the redefinition of the SI second to be completed first.
Boundary of credit relative to other contributors on magic-wavelength spectroscopy and Sr clock development, which I cannot verify independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Controlled trapped atoms and ions as quantum information processors began with the Cirac-Zoller gate proposal and its realization in ion-trap experiments. It opened quantum computation and simulation in atomic systems and connects directly to coherent light-matter control, a domain close to my own work.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the decisive theoretical proposals. Blatt provides experimental realization in ion traps with high-fidelity gates and entanglement. Bloch is the key figure for the optical-lattice simulation strand, but the three-name limit and the bundling of two strands make allocation difficult. Wineland's 2012 prize already covers ion control, which complicates the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed across many groups and now commercial platforms. The theoretical framework is stable. The overlap with 2012 and the 2022 entanglement prize means the novelty claim must be framed carefully, but timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 Wineland-Haroche prize and the 2022 Bell-test prize.
This candidate bundles several strands, atoms in traps and in lattices, and may need to be split.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum matter: a flat-band prediction, followed by correlated insulators and unconventional superconductivity. It created a very large and active field with a tunable platform for strongly correlated physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experimental discovery. This is a natural theory-plus-experiment three-person configuration. Other members of the experimental team are not on the supplied credit list, which limits what I can propose.
assessment.maturity: The core observations have been reproduced by several groups, but the microscopic origin of superconductivity and the correlated states remains debated. Recognition may be somewhat premature for the pairing mechanism, though the discovery itself is solid.
uncertainties: Reproducibility depends on sample and twist-angle disorder.
Experimental credit beyond the listed names cannot be allocated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry turned matter-wave coherence into precision sensors for gravity, rotation and fundamental constants. It is a case where better measurement defines what physics can test, and it has become a central tool in quantum sensing and tests of the equivalence principle.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard, Mlynek and Kasevich each demonstrated early matter-wave interferometers (atoms and gratings), with Kasevich bringing in inertial-sensing precision. Other groups also contributed decisive demonstrations, so allocation is contested and the three-name limit is a real constraint.
assessment.maturity: Widely confirmed across many laboratories and in applications; ongoing improvements, such as large-momentum-transfer interferometers, continue. Recognition would be timely, although laser cooling (1997) and BEC (2001) prizes cover adjacent ground.
uncertainties: Substantial disputed credit across several early groups.
Degree of overlap with prior atomic-physics prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators, from Kane-Mele's theory to the HgTe experiment of Molenkamp's group, is conceptually clean and led to a broad topological-materials field. The experimental observation of edge conduction is a clear signature.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction; the HgTe proposal by other theorists and the experimental observation under Molenkamp are also decisive, but the proposers of the HgTe scheme are not in the supplied names. The 2016 Nobel Prize covered topological phase transitions, so this must be shown as a distinct discovery.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed in HgTe and InAs/GaSb, with 3D topological insulators and ARPES studies widely reproduced. Mature.
uncertainties: Missing credit to the HgTe theory proposal, outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED supplies strong coupling between superconducting qubits and microwave resonators, enabling readout, gates and a leading platform for quantum processors. It is a highly consequential light-matter coupling demonstration in an engineered solid-state system.
assessment.attribution: Blais and colleagues' theoretical proposal, with Wallraff and Schoelkopf's 2004 experimental demonstration, supports a three-person configuration. Credit for the underlying qubits is a separate matter.
assessment.maturity: The platform is thoroughly confirmed and is scaling, but a recent Nobel prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits means the committee has just addressed an adjacent area, so timing is delicate.
uncertainties: Proximity to the recent superconducting-circuit prize.
Whether the committee would prefer to wait for demonstrated fault tolerance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube discovery of a diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux and the identification of TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane as sources opened neutrino astronomy. A major, clearly defined observational result.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube; Karle and Spiering held key detector and analysis leadership roles. Credit within a collaboration of hundreds is hard to apportion, and instrument leadership versus analysis discovery remains unresolved.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is robustly confirmed; source identification is still being strengthened, though the discovery claim itself is stable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy spins in diamond created a room-temperature solid-state quantum sensor with nanoscale magnetic, electric and thermal sensitivity. This fits the idea that progress is limited by what can be measured and how accurately, and it has reached biology and materials physics.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko demonstrated single-NV optical detection and coherent control; Lukin's group contributed key sensing and quantum-register demonstrations. Other groups are also decisive, so the three-name credit is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have confirmed the basic physics, with sensing applications growing, but the applied impact is still developing and some milestones may be better judged after more years.
uncertainties: Fair credit among several competing early groups.
Whether sensing impact is mature enough compared with the platform's quantum-register role.
